sovereign_country.strategic_role: 拉美美元金融中枢、私人利益基金会（PIF）与运河船舶登记

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Serialized Digital Web Fiction and Interactive Reading App

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Hybrid (Civil Law foundation with strong Anglo-American corporate law elements in the Sociedad Anónima regime)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Panama–United States Trade Promotion Agreement (TPA, in force 2012)
Panama–Republic of Korea Bilateral Investment Treaty (2021)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Ley 23 de 27 de abril de 2015 (as amended by Ley 52 de 2016, Ley 70 de 2019 and Ley 129 de 2020); Decreto Ejecutivo 363 de 2015; Resolución UAF No. 1771 de 2015; Law 254 of 12 November 2021 (Registro de Transparencia y Beneficiarios Finales); Law 41 of 2000 (anti-money laundering); Law 2 of 2011 (financing of terrorism); corporate governance under Law 32 of 1927 (Sociedades Anónimas) and Executive Decree 660 of 2019.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of passport of each proposed director, officer and ultimate beneficial owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: National Passport Authority / Notary Public of the country of origin

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Special Power of Attorney (Poder Especial) authorizing the Panamanian registered agent and attorney to incorporate the Sociedad Anónima
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary Public in the country of origin

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing (Certificado de Persona Jurídica) for any corporate shareholder of the entity to be incorporated
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Corporate Registry of the shareholder's home jurisdiction

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incumbency / Register of Directors for any corporate shareholder and proof of authority of signatory
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Corporate Secretary or Registered Agent of the shareholder entity

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all directors, officers and ultimate beneficial owners against the OFAC SDN List, United Nations Security Council consolidated sanctions list, UAF Panama National Terrorist and Sanctions Lists, EU and UK consolidated sanctions lists, and domestic politically exposed persons databases under Article 47 and 48 of Law 23 of 2015 and UAF Resolution No. 1771/2015; enhanced due diligence is mandatory for PEPs and family members/close associates; ongoing transaction and UBO monitoring records must be retained for a minimum of five (5) years after termination of the business relationship.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registro Público de Panamá – Sede Electrónica (eRegistro), available at https://e.registro-publico.gob.pa; institutional portal www.registro-publico.gob.pa; related municipal licensing via Panamá Emprende (www.panamaemprende.gob.pa)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Corporate names must be submitted in Latin (Roman) script; Spanish-language names are preferred, and any non-Latin script name shall be transliterated phonetically into Latin characters; the name must be pronounceable in Spanish and ending with 'Sociedad Anónima' or the abbreviation 'S.A.', or an accepted equivalent such as 'Inc.' or 'Corp.' where permitted by the S.A. regime; special diacritics and characters that impede registry indexing must be transliterated or removed.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Banco / Bank / Bancario – requires prior authorization of the Superintendencia de Bancos de Panamá
Seguros / Insurance / Reaseguro – requires prior authorization of the Superintendencia de Seguros
Valores / Bolsa / Exchange – requires prior authorization of the Superintendencia del Mercado de Valores
Trust / Fideicomiso / Fiduciario – requires financial licensing
Nacional / Gobierno / Estado / Oficial – implies official sponsorship and is prohibited unless approved
Licores / Tabaco / Farmacia / Hospital – requires sectoral ministerial license or health authority approval
Tokens identical or deceptively similar to an existing corporate name recorded in the Registro Público
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection, the applicant may file a 'Recurso de Reconsideración' before the Director General del Registro Público within five (5) working days of notification, and subsequently a 'Recurso de Apelación' in the same administrative file pursuant to Law 38 of 2000 (Régimen Administrativo); an extension of a valid reservation (prórroga) may be requested before expiration for one additional 30-day period upon payment of the applicable tariff; if no extension is granted, the reservation lapses and a new name search and reservation procedure must be initiated.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permissible for the digital WebNovel business: no physical operational office in Panama is required for an online subscription platform; however, the Sociedad Anónima must permanently maintain a resident agent (Agente Residente) located at a physical Panamanian address where legal process may be served; a purely virtual registered office without a physical street address is not accepted, and the registered agent's physical office constitutes the registered address for official correspondence and service of process.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low – estimated at less than 10% annual probability for an ISIC 9000 low-risk digital subscription business in the first year of operation; the likelihood may increase to 15–20% if the company fails to file the annual franchise tax or municipal Aviso de Operación, if the resident agent is flagged on UAF risk matrices, or if irregularities appear in UBO declarations; UAF risk-based supervision permits unannounced inspections upon reasonable administrative trigger.

Notarial execution of the deed of incorporation (Escritura Pública de Incorporación)
Protocolization and inscription of the incorporation deed in the Public Registry
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Registro Público de Panamá – Departamento de Personas Jurídicas
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory registry tariff scale (base rate for Sociedad Anónima)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Resident agent services (Agente Residente), first annual term
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Licensed registered agent (law firm or authorized corporate agent)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Municipal Aviso de Operación (tax patent / operation notice) for digital services

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Apostille or consular legalization of the power of attorney and UBO documentary bundle

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory consular/apostille fee per document bundle

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Compliance and incorporation legal fees (full outsourcing package including AML/CFT UBO file preparation)

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Ley General de Sociedades (Law 32 of 1927, as amended, and its enabling regulations), specifically Articles 1–150 governing Sociedades Anónimas (Corporations)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registro Público de Panamá (Public Registry of Panama), Mercantile Section
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Escritura Pública (Public Deed) containing the Pacto Social and Estatutos (Articles of Incorporation and By-Laws)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital; the authorized capital must be stated in the Articles but may be uncalled and unissued. No escrow account is required for incorporation.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the corporation hereby accepts the subscription of shares to the initial shareholders as set forth in the Articles of Incorporation. FURTHER RESOLVED, that the registered office of the corporation be established at the address designated in the by-laws, and that the registered agent be appointed in compliance with Panamanian law. FURTHER RESOLVED, that the following officers are duly appointed: President, Secretary, and Treasurer, each authorized to act with customary corporate authority. The Board directs these officers to execute all documents, open banking accounts, and secure all fiscal, municipal, and operational registrations required to commence lawful operations. All matters presented at this meeting are hereby approved.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate Name Reservation and Availability Search
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Público de Panamá – Online Services Portal (Sistema de Reserva de Nombre)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit an online application for a name reservation of the proposed corporate name (e.g., 'NovelaWeb Digital, S.A.'). Provide three alternative names in order of preference. The system shall indicate conflicts, and the successful name is reserved for 30 days, renewable for an additional 30 days upon payment of the statutory fee.
required_dossiers: Application form for name reservation (digital)
Photographic identification of the applicant or legal representative
Power of attorney if the applicant is acting on behalf of a third party
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected due to similarity to an existing entity, immediately submit the next alternative name. If sampling indicates trademark conflict, the applicant may file a statutory challenge with the Registry; alternatively, adopt a distinct distinctive name and amend the application.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Notarization of Articles of Incorporation and By-Laws
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary Public of the Republic of Panama (Notaría Pública)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Pacto Social (articles of incorporation) and Estatutos (by-laws). The document must state the corporate name, registered office location, object (to operate a digital web fiction platform), capital structure (authorized shares, classes, par value), resident agent of record, and governing board structure. The incorporators must appear before a Panamanian notary to execute the deed, certifying the signatures and pagination.
required_dossiers: Reserved corporate name certificate
Draft of the Articles of Incorporation and By-Laws in Spanish
Passports or identity cards of all subscribing shareholders and initial directors
Power of attorney (notarized, apostilled, and translated) if any incorporator acts by proxy
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary identifies legal inconsistencies (e.g., insufficient share classification or omissions of required clauses), correct the draft and re-execute the deed. The notary may charge an additional fee for rewriting; resumption is immediate once amendments are made.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registration of Public Deed at the Public Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Público de Panamá (Mercantile Section) or via a certified attorney with registry credentials
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the notarized Escritura Pública with the Public Registry for inscription. The Registry will review the deed for statutory compliance, legal existence, and adequate address/agent information. Upon approval, the corporation is officially registered and provided a Registry Number (microficha number).
required_dossiers: Notarized Escritura Pública (original and one certified copy)
Copy of the name reservation certificate
Proof of payment of registry filing fees (official receipt)
Affidavit of acceptance (diligencia de aceptación) from the appointed resident agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Public Registry issues a defect notice (nota de defecto), resolve deficiencies by filing a corrective brief within the prescribed 60-day cure period. Pay any applicable surcharge or refile the deed if the defect is substantive. If the registry rejects the name due to trademark conflict, initiate a challenge or amend the corporate name and proceed with a new deed.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtaining Taxpayer Identification Number (RUC) and Fiscal Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) – Ministry of Economy and Finance; online portal DGI Digital
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After incorporation, register the S.A. with the DGI to obtain the Registro Único de Contribuyente (RUC). Provide the official registry inscription and corporate documents. The entity shall be registered for income tax, ITBMS (value added tax), and any applicable advance tax; note that Panama applies a territorial tax system, but the digital platform must still file annual reports.
required_dossiers: Certified copy of the registered Escritura Pública
Certified copy of the Public Registry inscription
Corporate officers' identification documents (passports, for non-residents)
Completed DGI Form 101 (Solicitud de RUC)
Proof of registered office address (e.g., lease, utility bill, or registered agent affidavit)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the DGI imposes an unanticipated tax classification or requests additional information, respond within 15 business days with amendments. Non-resident shareholders must provide tax residency certificates if claiming treaty relief. If registration is delayed, request a temporary RUC pending final issuance while ensuring all transactions are recorded.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Municipal Business Permit and Non-Financial Operating License
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Municipality of Panama (Alcaldía de Panamá) – Department of Business Activities (Aviso de Operación)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply for an Aviso de Operación (Business Operation Notice) at the municipal level. Since this is a digital content platform with no physical storefront, the application should be categorized as 'Electronic Commerce – Digital Content Provider' and require no special industry permit. The municipality will assess an annual business tax based on declared capital and projected revenue; renew the permit each January 31.
required_dossiers: Copy of the RUC certificate
Copy of the Public Registry inscription
Corporate by-laws and officer list
Proof of ownership or lease for the registered physical office address (of Panamanian registered agent)
Completed municipal application form and payment receipt for Aviso de Operación
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: For municipal inquiry, submit a written explanation clarifying that the activity is a virtual subscription platform, not requiring physical premises beyond a registered address. If the tax coefficient is excessive, appeal within the municipality within 30 days providing financial data to recalculate the rate.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: No applicable industrial licensing authority for the operation of a serialized digital web fiction platform. If the company later establishes physical offices, the competent authority would be the Ministry of Labor and Occupational Health (MITRADEL) for workplace permits.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No dedicated operating license required. The company operates under the municipal 'Aviso de Operación' and its general corporate registration.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministerio de Ambiente (Ministry of Environment of Panama) – Environmental Impact Assessment Directorate
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt – Category IV: The activity is a purely digital, non-industrial operation with no physical production, waste emission, or natural resource usage. No EIA report, registration, or baseline study is required.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Non-applicable. The platform generates no wastewater, volatile organic compounds, hazardous waste, or atmospheric emissions. All computing services are hosted on third-party cloud infrastructure; however, if the company acquires physical servers, they must comply with residual electronic waste disposal regulations under Resolution No. AG-0417-2020 and the General Law on Waste (Law 12 of 2021).

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not required for a digital platform with no physical operational premises. When the company secures a representative office, it must obtain a fire safety certificate and an occupancy permit from the Panama City Fire Department (Cuerpo de Bomberos) and a structural inspection by the Ministry of Housing and Land Planning (MIVIOT) for any office open to the public or employees; for the current registered office (a law firm / registered agent address), only a duly filed sworn declaration of use is needed.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) of the Ministry of Economy and Finance (MEF); online taxpayer portal is the 'Sistema E-Tax' at https://etax.dgi.gob.pa, with general guidance at www.dgi.gob.pa
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: After incorporation of the Sociedad Anónima in the Registro Público, the resident legal representative (or a registered public accountant with power of attorney) must file the RUC (Registro Único de Contribuyente) application with the DGI, submitting the corporate charter, appointment resolution, and identity documents of shareholders and legal representative. The DGI assigns the RUC number, activates the taxpayer as 'Activo', issues the RUC certification with authentication code, and sets the tax regime and CAIP activity code. The applicant must also obtain the municipal Aviso de Operación before starting operations. Foreign shareholders are not required to appear in person; the local legal representative completes the procedure. No minimum capital is required, and the entire registration can be completed electronically through Sistema E-Tax with digital signature.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box election akin to the US regime exists. The S.A. is automatically a separate taxable person taxed at entity level only on Panama-source income under the territorial provisions of the Código Fiscal (Arts. 694 and 700). A qualifying corporation may elect into the 'Régimen de Tributación para Operaciones Internacionales' (Law 254 of 2021) for defined international activities, subject to economic substance and notification requirements. Small taxpayers with gross income below the ITBMS threshold may elect the simplified small-taxpayer treatment (pago definitivo). Taxpayers may also elect between the general ITBMS method and the simplified ITBMS method where eligible, and may voluntarily register for ITBMS despite falling under the threshold.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: ITBMS (Impuesto de Transferencia de Bienes Muebles y Servicios), a value-added tax levied under Decree Law 8 of 2010
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: PAB 36,000 (equivalent to USD 36,000) of annual gross revenue from taxable activities; registration becomes mandatory once the threshold is exceeded or upon the first importation of taxable goods, while registration is voluntary below the threshold
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Panama has progressively mandated the 'Régimen de Facturación Electrónica de Panamá (RFEP)' pursuant to Law 8 of 2010 and DGI implementing resolutions. All ITBMS-registered taxpayers integrate with the DGI through the official 'Facturador Electrónico' (the DGI's free web facturador, a commercial certified facturador, or a direct API/web-service connection to the DGI's E-Tax clearance platform). Every invoice and credit note must be transmitted to the DGI in real time for automated validation; the DGI issues a unique digital authorization and tracking code (código de seguimiento) that must appear on the printed invoice alongside a QR code. For low-value consumer sales executed through Apple IAP and Google Play Billing, the platform must issue a simplified electronic VAT receipt, referencing the app-store transaction ID, for each sale; munitions, alcohol, tobacco, and gambling carry differentiated rates (10% and 15%) not applicable to digital content.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: A 0% ITBMS rate applies to exports of goods and to services rendered to non-resident persons or effectively consumed outside Panama, including serialized web fiction subscriptions and in-app digital content sold to foreign users. To qualify, the taxpayer must be ITBMS-registered and demonstrate that the digital service was supplied to a non-resident customer and paid for from abroad. Evidentiary criteria include the foreign user's registration country, IP-address and geolocation analytics, foreign billing address, app-store payout remittances received from Apple/Google, and contractual terms disqualifying Panama-based consumption; the export claim must be supported by corresponding foreign exchange receipts and a reconciliation of platform gross sales against tax returns.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Declaración de Exportación) where goods are involved; for digital services, the zero-rated export invoice and platform settlement reports substitute for the customs declaration
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill for physical exports; for digital services, platform download logs and app-store transaction reports serve as evidence of cross-border delivery
Inward Remittance Certificate, SWIFT credit advice, or app-store payout statement evidencing collection of the export price from abroad
Export invoice annotated with the 0% ITBMS rate and the customer's foreign VAT/identification number where available
Service contract or Terms of Use binding the foreign end user to consumption outside Panama
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The DGI may scrutinize export declarations, ITBMS refund claims, and digital platform records; where zero-rating is claimed without adequate proof of foreign consumption or the service is found to be enjoyed in Panama, the DGI retroactively assesses the 7% ITBMS plus monthly interest and surcharges, with surcharges of up to 200% of the omitted tax for fraudulent or bad-faith filings. Fines per unsubstantiated invoice typically range from PAB 100 to PAB 10,000, the taxpayer's export authorization may be suspended, and the knowing issuance of false export documentation triggers criminal prosecution under Law 14 of 2004 (tax criminal code), which carries custodial penalties.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Panama does not have a central bank; the US dollar is legal tender under the Monetary Agreement with the United States. Banking activities are supervised by the Superintendencia de Bancos de Panamá (SBP), and the Ministry of Economy and Finance (MEF) oversees fiscal matters. No foreign exchange administration exists.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Full convertibility is inherent as the US dollar circulates as legal tender; the Panamanian Balboa exists only as a fractional unit at a 1:1 peg. Both current and capital account transactions are unrestricted with no prior approval, exchange control, or profit remittance restrictions. Dividends, royalties, and service fees may be freely transferred abroad.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: There are no statutory surrender requirements, mandatory conversion ratios, or timelines for export/earnings repatriation. All proceeds may be retained in any currency and remitted without central bank approval, consistent with Panama's dollarized, open capital account regime.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Medium-High, subject to legal constraints. Panama's regulatory framework does not yet explicitly recognize standalone 'electronic money institutions' (EMIs). Digital payment providers generally require a banking license or an alliance with a licensed bank. Offshore digital EMIs (e.g., non-Panamanian entities) cannot directly hold accounts in Panama's domestic banking system without a local presence or partnered bank. Operational viability is moderate for cross-border settlement via prepaid cards and payment gateways, but restrictions apply to accepting deposits or issuing electronic money without SBP authorization.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physically meeting a bank officer is generally mandatory for opening corporate accounts in Panama. Under SBP Rule No. 004-2017 (AML/CFT) and standard bank policies, beneficial owners and legal representatives must appear in person at a local branch, provide original identification, and co-sign account forms. Remote opening is permitted only in exceptional circumstances for non-resident clients with strong pre-existing bank relationships, but in practice all Tier-1 Panamanian banks currently require an in-country interview or a banking relationship via a trusted intermediary with power-of-attorney verified by a Panamanian notary.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Foreign entity with non-resident shareholders and no physical office in Panama
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certificate of Incorporation and bylaws apostilled by the origin country; certified resolutions appointing signatories; notarized power-of-attorney valid in Panama; detailed business plan describing the web novel platform; source of funds evidence (e.g., published annual financial statements or audited accounts for the parent or investor); bank references from a regulated institution in the home jurisdiction; passport copies and proof of residential address for each beneficial owner (e.g., utility bill or bank statement within 3 months).

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Flow of funds from app stores (Apple/Google) routed via third-party payment processors
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed agreements with Apple, Google, or payment gateway providers; flow-of-funds diagram showing settlement cycles and fees; a list of expected counterparties and countries (to assess jurisdictional risk); evidence of RBT (remote business-to-business) verification, such as a registered trademark or copyright registration for the digital content; monthly reconciliation statements from the platform operator to prove the origin of funds.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Holding company structure with intermediate entities in high-risk or opaque jurisdictions
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Full corporate chain chart from ultimate beneficial owner (UBO) to the Panamanian S.A.; certified register of members/shareholders; share certificates evidencing the percentage of beneficial ownership; for any intermediate entity in a high-risk jurisdiction, a legal opinion confirming legitimate purpose and adequate substance; AML/CFT policies of the group (if applicable); sworn declaration of UBOs confirming no politically exposed person (PEP) status unless disclosed.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital injections (shareholder loans or equity) must be routed via standard SWIFT wire transfers to the Panama corporate account. No FX approval is required. The remittance should include clear payment purpose codes (e.g., 'Investment – Share Capital' and 'Intragroup Loan') and reference the Panamanian entity's RUC (tax ID). Supporting documents (shareholder resolution, loan agreement, or capital contribution deed) must be retained to comply with bank KYC/AML verification. The bank will typically perform a 'source of wealth' inquiry for amounts above USD 10,000 and may place a temporary hold pending compliance review.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound disbursements for trade settlements use SWIFT MT103 for direct wire transfers and Commercial Letters of Credit (LC) for documentary transactions. MT103 messages require detailed beneficiary bank codes (BIC/IBAN), and payment purpose codes aligned with the OCIMF/ISO 20022 standard (e.g., 'Royalty Payment', 'Digital Content License Fee', 'Software Services') when the bank supports structured remittance. For higher-value payments (e.g., content licensing to foreign authors or platform technology providers), banks may request underlying contracts and proof of service delivery. Commercial LC issuance is feasible for physical trade, but for digital web novel subscriptions, MT103 wires are the standard clearing rail.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Plain-vanilla deliverable forwards (FX forwards) between USD and major currencies, executed via SBP-regulated banks or international broker dealers without requiring prior authorization.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for exotic-currency exposure (e.g., emerging market currencies) may be arranged by international banks, provided the Panamanian entity is a professional counterparty and the bank's internal suitability criteria are met.

Cross-currency swaps (FX swaps / interest rate swaps) are permissible for treasury management, subject to standard documentation (ISDA Master Agreement) and regulatory compliance under Panamanian banking practice.
Options on foreign currencies (call/put options) are available through licensed international brokers. No derivative transaction is subject to exchange control approval in Panama.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual franchise-fee payment and electronic return (Tasa Única Anual) for the Sociedad Anónima
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministerio de Comercio e Industrias (MICI) through the Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) e-Tax portal; coordinated by the Panamanian registered agent
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually between 1 January and 30 April for calendar-year companies; anniversary-based window if a foreign fiscal year is elected
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late payment attracts a 10% statutory surcharge plus monthly default interest under Law 2 of 2011; unpaid fees for five or more consecutive years expose the S.A. to administrative strike-off and cancellation of registration in the Registro Público.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income-tax declaration (Declaración Jurada de Renta), filed as a territorial-source, zero-return, or operative return as applicable
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: DGI – Dirección General de Ingresos (Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas), online fiscal portal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually by 31 March following the 31 December fiscal year-end; a three-month statutory filing window applies for calendar-year taxpayers
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to timely file triggers fines of B/.50 to B/.5,000 under the Código Fiscal, plus default interest and a 10% late-payment surcharge on any Panamanian-source tax due; DGI may suspend the Paz y Salvo tax-clearance certificate.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual confirmation of ultimate beneficial ownership information (Declaración Anual de Beneficiario Final)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: DGI Beneficial-Ownership Registry (Registro de Beneficiarios Finales), e-Tax online module
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually by 31 March for the preceding fiscal year; any shareholding or UBO change must be reported within 30 calendar days of the event
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-compliance carries entity-level fines of B/.5,000 to B/.50,000; knowingly false or withheld UBO data is subject to fines of B/.50,000 to B/.100,000 under Law 129 of 2020 and implementing decrees.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Record of the annual ordinary shareholders' meeting in the corporate minute book, if required by the bylaws
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: No external filing; corporate records retained at the registered office in Panama
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within the period fixed by the bylaws; absent a bylaw term, Law 32 of 1927 imposes no fixed statutory date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Omission does not constitute a state filing penalty but weakens evidentiary standing of corporate acts and may impair administrative good standing in due-diligence reviews.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent audit applies where a Panama S.A. reports gross annual income above USD 1,000,000, holds total assets above USD 2,000,000, or operates as a Panama-regulated financial, insurance, or public-interest entity; other low-risk digital-content entities may remain below the compulsory-audit threshold.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS (NIIF) as adopted in Panama; IFRS for SMEs is permissible for entities below the public-interest threshold; a U.S. GAAP basis may be accepted for foreign-parented groups with DGI consent.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The S.A. must maintain a current beneficial-ownership file and submit an annual DGI confirmation for all natural-person ultimate beneficial owners even if no shareholding has changed; any share transfer or UBO variation must be reported within 30 calendar days, supported by updated extracts of the share register and identity documentation.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Minute Book (Libro de Actas de Junta Directiva y Accionistas)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 250 – 650 per annum for a Panamanian registered agent and registered-office service, excluding the USD 300 government franchise fee
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 2,500 – 8,000 for a certified independent audit of a low-risk digital-content S.A. at or above the compulsory threshold; USD 1,200 – 2,500 for a below-threshold compilation or review engagement

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Preferential 15% rate applies to the first USD 50,000 of Panamanian-source net taxable income; excess taxed at 25%. Territorial taxation exempts foreign-source income derived from digital subscription services where the economic activity, contract execution, and utilization occur outside Panama. No general statutory tax holiday for webnovel platforms; certain regime-based incentives (SEM Headquarters, Panama Pacifico, Ciudad del Saber) are inapplicable absent special licensing. ITBMS (VAT) 7% is zero-rated on exported services. NOL deduction allowed for 5 years.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Formulario 100 (Declaración Anual de Renta de Personas Jurídicas) filed electronically through DGI's Sedi e-filing portal (Sistema de Declaraciones, Impuestos y Cobros) using the company's RUC (Registro Único de Contribuyentes) credentials.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual; quarterly advance income tax payments (pagos directos) due 15 June, 15 September, 15 December, and 15 March; monthly ITBMS return (Form 202) for registered merchants.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Form 100 is due during March of the year immediately following the fiscal year-end, with the exact date assigned by DGI according to the last digit of the RUC (generally between 1 March and 31 March). A fiscal year different from the calendar year may be elected by the S.A. only with prior DGI approval.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Company RUC, fiscal period, corporate name, and registered address of the Sociedad Anónima.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident shareholders have no filing obligation for Form 100; the Panamanian S.A. is the resident taxpayer. The resident agent's address must be recorded as fiscal address.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total gross revenue recognized under Panama GAAP, including all worldwide receipts before deductions; for the webnovel platform, include App Store and Google Play settlement amounts (net of platform commissions) plus advertisement and licensing revenue.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the non-resident beneficial owner directly earns subscription income through a Panamanian S.A. acting as a conduit, DGI may recharacterize; the gross amount must be reported regardless of where the foreign shareholders reside.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 2 - Ingresos exentos y no gravables
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Foreign-source income excluded under Panama's territorial tax regime; includes subscription and digital content revenue derived from services rendered and economically utilized outside Panama, supported by contracts, user location data, and payment-rail settlement reports.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Exemption is allowed only where the service is rendered abroad and the payor is located abroad. App Store revenues from Panamanian consumers must be reclassified as Panamanian-source and taxed at 25%; documentary substantiation (geo-IP, customer billing addresses, foreign content distribution agreements) must be retained.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deductible operating expenditures directly attributable to the production of gross income: content author royalties, translation and editing costs, server hosting, app maintenance, marketing, legal, and administrative expenses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Expenses are deductible only when economically linked to Panamanian-source income. If the entity's foreign-source income is exempt, related expenses must be proportionally excluded. Payments to foreign related parties for royalties or services must be arm's length and supported by transfer pricing documentation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net operating loss deduction (NOL) carried forward from prior fiscal years; Panama permits a maximum carryforward of 5 years.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: NOLs arising in Panama may offset only Panamanian-source income; losses of foreign branches or foreign disregarded entities cannot be transferred to the Panamanian S.A.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net taxable income after exempt revenues and allowable deductions; this is the tax base for the progressive corporate rate.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident company without a permanent establishment in Panama is not assessed on Panama-source income unless it operates through a fixed base; the resident S.A. must nevertheless compute this line under the territorial rules.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax at 15% on the first USD 50,000 of net taxable income and 25% on the excess over USD 50,000.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident shareholders cannot offset their home-country tax credits against Panama's corporate ITBMS credited; the corporate tax is an entity-level liability.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Credits including quarterly advance payments (pagos directos), third-party withholding certificates, and ITBMS credits deductible against income tax.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign tax credits are not granted by Panama; credit is limited to domestic withholdings and presumed dividend credits. Payments made to non-residents without Panamanian withholding will not generate creditable withholding.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 10 - Impuesto a pagar / saldo a favor
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Excess of Box 8 over Box 9; balance due must be paid on filing. A saldo a favor may be claimed as a credit or refund via separate DGI procedure.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The company cannot avoid tax by retaining earnings; undistributed taxable profits may trigger the presumed-dividend tax (10%) of the annual taxable income when distributions are made to foreign shareholders.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing or non-filing: monthly surcharge of 10% of the tax due per month or fraction, capped at 50% of the tax; late payment interest accrues at the statutory rate referenced to the Banco Nacional de Panamá rate; repeated non-filing within 12 months triggers an additional administrative fine up to USD 5,000, the suspension of the paz y salvo (tax clearance), and the loss of good standing with the Public Registry; continued delinquency may lead to administrative dissolution and referral to the tax crimes prosecutor.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 10% on dividends paid out of Panamanian-source taxable profits (5% for dividends from shares registered on a recognized Panamanian or regional stock exchange); 10% withholding also applies to dividends paid out of tax-exempt income; dividends sourced entirely from foreign-source profits are exempt from Panamanian dividend tax.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Panama maintains a limited DTA network. To invoke treaty relief, the non-resident beneficial owner must deliver a Certificate of Tax Residence (TRC) issued by the tax authority of the treaty state, with official Spanish translation and apostille where applicable, to the withholding agent before the distribution date. The withholding agent must enter the treaty-eligible rate in the annual withholding return (Form 170), attach the TRC, and retain the TRC and supporting ownership evidence for 5 years. Supplemental forms (Form 171 for monthly remittances and the refund application) are processed through DGI's Sedi portal. Failure to obtain the TRC in advance results in application of the statutory 10% dividend WHT.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties and technical service fees paid to non-residents for Panamanian-source IP use are subject to 12.5% statutory WHT (for certain technical services the taxable base is reduced to 50% of gross, producing a 6.25% effective rate). Interest paid to non-residents is generally subject to 12.5% WHT when paid by the Panamanian entity to a foreign related lender, while interest on registered external debt and bank credit lines may be exempt. Under applicable DTAs, rates may be reduced to 5%-15% for royalties and 5%-10% for interest upon TRC-based treaty claim.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: USD (Balboa at 1:1 with USD). Mandatory Local File: taxpayer whose gross income or total assets exceeded USD 2,000,000 in the fiscal year, or which transacts with related parties. Mandatory Master File: multinational group whose consolidated revenue exceeded USD 50,000,000. Country-by-Country Report: group consolidated revenue of at least USD 850,000,000. Documentation must be prepared within 6 months after the fiscal year-end and submitted to DGI upon request.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Panama's Economic Substance Requirements (Law 70 of 2019, effective for fiscal years beginning after 1 July 2020) apply to entities deriving income from relevant activities, including IP holding, distribution and services, and pure equity holding. A webnovel platform S.A. exploiting copyrighted content and earning subscription/licensing income is in scope. The entity must demonstrate that core income-generating activities (contract negotiation, billing, IP exploitation, server/content management decisions) are conducted in Panama, maintain a physical office and adequate qualified staff, and file the annual Declaration of Economic Substance with DGI. Non-compliance may trigger penalties up to USD 500,000, and the DGI may notify the Public Registry, effectively blocking the entity from conducting commercial activities.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Willfully misclassifying Panamanian-source App Store receipt revenue as foreign-source income, under-reporting gross subscription income, or omitting Form 100 for consecutive years while distributing profits to foreign shareholders.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal conviction carries imprisonment of 2 to 5 years; financial penalty of up to 3 times the evaded tax; monthly surcharges of 10% (capped at 50%) plus late-payment interest; DGI has the power to embargo bank accounts and publish the taxpayer on the official delinquency registry.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and the legal representative who signed false returns face personal criminal prosecution, civil restitution of evaded taxes, asset embargoes, and travel bans (salida del país) imposed by the Fiscal Crimes Prosecutor while proceedings are pending.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Paying excessive royalties or service fees to a connected IP-holding company in a zero-tax jurisdiction with no economic substance, producing sustained taxable losses in Panama or a gross margin below the arm's length range for digital content distributors.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: DGI recharacterizes the related-party consideration, assesses the adjustment at the 25% corporate rate, applies a surcharge of 40% of the understatement where TP documentation was not filed, and imposes fines up to USD 50,000 for non-submission of the TP return or documentation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly approved non-arm's length agreements are jointly liable for the additional corporate tax; if the company is insolvent, directors face civil liability under the S.A. law for breach of fiduciary duty and fraudulent transfer actions.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating the platform as a pure 'letterbox' S.A. with no office, no employees, and no economic decision-making in Panama while engaging in relevant activities (IP holding, digital distribution and services) and failing to file the annual Economic Substance Return.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: ESR monetary penalties from USD 5,000 to USD 500,000 per fiscal year; repeat or aggravated offenses can lead to the suspension of the commercial matrícula, the loss of tax residence status, and delisting from the Public Registry.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and the resident agent are jointly and severally liable for the ESR annual filing obligation; the resident agent faces administrative sanctions and potential loss of accreditation, while directors may be personally assessed for penalties if they concealed the entity's activity.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using bearer shares or opaque nominee structures to conceal the ultimate beneficial owners of the webnovel platform while moving App Store settlement funds through Panama, or failing to file the Mandatory Beneficial Owner Declaration (Declaración de Beneficiario Final) within the statutory deadline.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Monetary fines from USD 1,000 to USD 50,000 for false, late, or omitted beneficial ownership declarations; where the structure facilitates money laundering, Law 23 of 2015 (as reformed) imposes imprisonment of 5 to 10 years and fines up to USD 5,000,000; the bank account and the corporation are listed on the UAF financial intelligence watchlist.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors, the resident agent, and any shareholder acting as a front signatory face criminal prosecution for money laundering and organized crime participation; the corporate veil is pierced for restitution, funds are seized, and principals are subject to INTERPOL red notices and extradition proceedings.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Paying dividends to a non-resident sole shareholder without withholding the 10% dividend tax and without filing Form 102 (Dividend Return), or distributing profits while the company remains in default on its Form 100 obligations.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: DGI assesses against the company the full 10% dividend withholding tax, plus monthly surcharges of 10% capped at 50% and statutory interest; the presumed-dividend regime may tax 10% of an imputed profit base when no timely return was filed; criminal referral follows for intentional omission.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are personally liable as withholding agents ('agentes de retención') for the un-withheld tax; DGI may initiate civil recovery against directors' personal assets, obtain travel bans, and, in cases of fraudulent bankruptcy, request imprisonment of up to 4 years.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Selling subscriptions to Panamanian consumers through Apple IAP and Google Play Billing without registering as a digital services provider, collecting the 7% ITBMS, or filing monthly Form 202.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Assessment of 7% ITBMS on taxable Panamanian digital sales, monthly surcharges of 5% up to a maximum of 100%, and fines for omitted tax up to 100% of the liability on repeated violations; DGI may order the payment gateways to suspend distribution of settlement funds.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The legal representative is jointly responsible for ITBMS remittances and faces criminal charges for destruction of consumption records and false invoicing; civil liability extends to the Board where revocation of the paz y salvo blocks future repatriation of dividends.
